snippet.textDisplay: This year’s In Memoriam segment was really tough to watch. Obviously, the loss of legends like Catherine O’Hara, Rob Reiner, and Dolly Parton cannot be overstated, but seeing Hayden Panettiere in particular and, correct me if I’m wrong, I believe she was the youngest person featured, made my heart sink. When the news broke, ngl, this was one of the few celebrity deaths where I had to sit down and take a few hours to process whether it was actually real because I love Hayden so much, like she’s the sister I never had, and I genuinely wish I could’ve done something to save her. Normally, I don’t worship celebrities like that, but Hayden always felt different to me; I know I never actually knew her, but her work meant so much to me, and I just wish she had gotten more time. Seeing her this soon in the In Memoriam segment just doesn’t sit well with me, but unfortunately, that’s the reality we have to accept, no matter how heartbreaking it is 💔

snippet.textDisplay: Noah Kahan’s performance of Bridge Over Troubled Water at this year’s Emmys was nothing short of breathtaking. Rather than simply covering the Simon & Garfunkel classic, he completely made it his own, delivering every line with extraordinary vulnerability, warmth and emotional depth. His raw, soulful voice, combined with the restrained beauty of the strings, transformed the song into a profoundly moving tribute. It was intimate yet monumental, beautifully understated yet utterly powerful. One of those rare performances that transcends the song itself and leaves an unforgettable emotional imprint. Simply phenomenal, hauntingly beautiful and absolutely sublime. ❤
